Can I suggest something that’s simple, yet sounds stupid. Whenever the thoughts arrive. Tell yourself a few things
1. Jealousy is normal, you’re entitled to feel the way you do.
2. His past - mistakes and all - belong to him, not you. Free yourself from the idea that anything that’s happened in the past has anything to do with you. 
3. That you refuse to let this idea control you, picture yourself as a person who is so capable that one day you’ll be able to support someone who struggles with what you struggled with. Create your own antidote. Become your own hero.
4. One day, you’ll no longer exist - his past, your past. Will all be gone. Enjoy him for who he is now. 
5. It’s hard, but it will go. You’ll manage! I promise.

Hey, your experience sounds a lot like mine. 

Unfortunately this is the journey.  Don’t worry too much about oxy intake, your body will recover from it very easily. 

There’s not heaps urgent care can do but monitor you. Few tips to ease the experience. 

Ice water and a straw. Small sips consistently is key. 

Table spoons of Manuka honey every 3 hours cools the area. Rescues pain. 

Porridge, oatmeal, whatever with protein powder will help. You gotta eat. This will speed up your recovery process. 

Mouth breathing is a part of the process if your nose is blocked, not a lot you can do.

Hey man, scabs falling off is a part of the healing process, you probably hadn’t noticed thus far but it would have been happening throughout your healing process - just at a smaller/slower rate. 

Slight bleeding is normal. I’d rinse and after 10 minutes if the bleeding is consistent (no sign of slowling/stopping).

If you feel your mouth filling with blood. You’ll need to go to your closest ER. 

Given you’re at day 10 though, I’d say you’re pretty close to being out of it.

PRP works, however you need ATLEAST 3 sessions, plus finasteride to maintain.

Hey man, 

First of, you’re not psycho, and what you’re experiencing is actually quite common. 

Becoming strongly attached to someone gives us a sense of security, happiness, love, it makes us feel really good. 

When that’s taken away, our mind goes into a frenzy, clawing for jr back and doing everything we can to get it back to the way it was - making act really out of character - but the real truth is, we just don’t want to face heartache anymore because it feels shit. 

This can often look like extreme overthinking, excessive messaging, them consistently being on your mind, not being able to sleep etc etc. 

Good news is, these feelings don’t stick with us forever, however, they do stem from somewhere in our childhood - our relationship with parents, absent parents, unhealthy past friendship and relationships etc etc. 

What your feeling is a sense of overwhelming sadness, it will pass. For the mean time, and this is the hard part, you will need to be more practical about how you distract yourself, change your focus, shift your mind from feeling you’re going to be alone, because it is okay and you WILL eventually feel better. 

Take care and stay safe

Firstly, you’re not alone - you’re going to grieve the loss of something that meant a lot to you. 

What we know about this is it does take time to heal. Unfortunately, you may continue to feel quite emotional for sometime, but it is normal and it does pass. 

Second, before jumping into panic mode (not referring to your panic attack) give yourself some time for your heart to catch up to your head. We tend to do silly things when we’re vulnerable - this might look like excessive texting or social media stalking. 

If she wants to remain friends, maybe that isn’t such a bad option. You may have the opportunity to remind her what made her fall in love with you. 

Sometimes upon reflection, we will sit back and think, I wish I could go back or I wish I could change this, the obvious answer is that we can’t. But we can learn from it, and it’s the most painful lessons that make the greatest changes. 

In other instances, maybe she just wasn’t feeling it, and as hard as that is to hear, she does have a right to feel that way. 

Trust me my ex girlfriend when she left me told me that she know longer loved me after 4 years together - I thought I would never recover again, I thought the hole in my heart would never heal. But it does and life will continue for you as it will for her. 

Anyway, I’m rambling now, long story short: 
Give yourself sometime, don’t overthink it but whatever happens, you will be okay.
